chunks.arabic_text: إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبَانَ بْنِ مَرَّارٍ، يَكْنَى أَبَا يَعْقُوبَ، الْأَحْمَرُ.

translations.en: Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Abān ibn Marrār, known by the kunya Abū Yaʿqūb, al-Aḥmar.

chunks.arabic_text: فَاسِدُ الْمَذْهَبِ، كَذَّابٌ فِي الرِّوَايَةِ، وَضَّاعٌ لِلْحَدِيثِ لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَى مَا رَوَاهُ، وَلَا يُرْتَفَعُ بِحَدِيثِهِ. وَلِلْعَيَّاشِيِّ مَعَهُ خَبَرٌ - فِي وَضْعِهِ لِلْحَدِيثِ - مَشْهُورٌ.

translations.en: Corrupt in madhhab. Liar in narration. Fabricator of ḥadīths. What he narrates is not regarded, and his ḥadīth are not to be given importance. Al-ʿAyyāshī has an incident with him regarding his fabrication of ḥadīths that is famous.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* classifies Isḥāq ibn al-Aḥmar as a *fāsid al-madhhab* (corrupt in creed) and a *kadhdhāb* (liar), indicating his narrations are *muṭawwāʿ* (reliable but not definitive) or *mawḍūʿ* (fabricated) depending on the specific context of his errors. The mention of al-ʿAyyāshī’s famous report highlights the rigorous cross-referencing in Shia *ʿilm al-rijāl*, where a single narrator’s weakness can be corroborated by multiple scholars to establish *al-waqf* (stopping reliance) on his transmissions. This classification serves as a critical filter for jurists evaluating the authenticity of hadiths transmitted through the chain of the Banū Abān.
en.seo_question: Who is Isḥāq al-Aḥmar and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
